title: The dubhan for Muileann bheag bought at Caol mhòr
summary: Peigi nic Ascaill, engineer to Comhairle nan Taighean-solais, buys the fuel for Taigh-solais Muileann bheag in the market at Caol mhòr, since no master will take a laden hull round the western capes in am Faoilleach. Twelve Tuathaich carts carry the barrels fifteen miles along the coast road to the tower. The carters are paid at the rate of the town.

title: The coal-store at Muileann bheag locked
summary: When Taigh-solais Muileann bheag is lit with dubhan, its keeper Calum Bàn, a Dia-thìreach of the south who has kept the light nineteen years, locks the last of its coal in the store at the tower's foot until Comhairle nan Taighean-solais shall say what is to be done with it.

title: The crane walked from Seann Tarr to Àth dhearg
summary: The rope-makers of Seann Tarr take down the crane of their rope-walk and carry it three and a half miles up the coast road to Taigh-solais Àth dhearg in pieces, on three wains. They raise it on the rock below the tower in two days and stay it to rings let into the stone. They will let no other hands touch their cables.

title: The rope-makers refuse hire for the crane
summary: When the tank of Taigh-solais Àth dhearg is set in its lamp-room, the rope-makers of Seann Tarr take their crane home and will take no hire for it. Their master sends word that the light owes them nothing, since their boats steer home by it. The keeper Iseabail Ruadh names the rope-walk in her daybook.

title: Peigi nic Ascaill writes to Caol mhòr for fitters
summary: Peigi nic Ascaill writes to Comhairle nan Taighean-solais that she cannot turn the light at Baile chrom before the autumn gales with the two fitters it can spare. In her own name she writes to the speaker at Caol mhòr, asking four Tuathaich fitters of the town for the work and a man named Ashby among them. She does not say who will pay them.

title: Four fitters of Caol mhòr walk to Baile chrom
summary: Daniel Frayne, speaker of Tional nan Tuathach, sends four fitters of Caol mhòr to turn the light at Baile chrom: Joe Ashby, Will Tanner and the cousins Ned and Abel Fowler. They walk the twenty-five miles in two days of rain. The tank and fuel come round by sea from Seann Skell and are landed below the headland.

title: The Tuathaich fitters paid by Tional nan Tuathach
summary: The clerk of Tional nan Tuathach at Caol mhòr pays the four fitters who turned the light at Baile chrom from the assembly's chest, for nine days' work and four days' walking, and enters their names and the sum in its book. He writes to Comhairle nan Taighean-solais for the money, and enters the sum as owed.

title: The keeper's report pinned at Caol mhòr
summary: The quarter-day report of Uilleam mac Dhòmhnaill, keeper of Taigh-solais Baile chrom, is copied by Comhairle nan Taighean-solais and sent round the shires. At Caol mhòr the maor pins it outside the custom-house. It says the light burns well and the town gives no trouble, and that the work was done by fitters from Caol mhòr. It names none of them.

title: Peigi nic Ascaill takes service with the works
summary: Peigi nic Ascaill leaves the service of Comhairle nan Taighean-solais at the end of the summer and takes service as master-fitter with Obair-dhubhain Seann Skell, the shipmasters' works on the south coast, which are building a second range of retorts.

title: Joe Ashby hired at the works
summary: Joe Ashby of Caol mhòr goes south in an t-Sultain at Peigi nic Ascaill's letter and is hired as a fitter at the shipmasters' works at Seann Skell on the south coast, with Ned and Abel Fowler. He is given a room over the forge. Will Tanner stays at Caol mhòr with his boat.

title: The first dubhan pit-lamps of Muileann mhin
summary: The lamp-makers of Muileann mhin, working from a burner drawn by Peigi nic Ascaill, make their first twelve pit-lamps to burn dubhan. Orders come for a hundred, from the pits still worked, from the yards of Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn and from the inns of the old roads. The guild will not yet stamp them with its mark.

title: Two fitters sign the lamp-makers' petition
summary: At the guild's hall of Muileann mhin, Peigi nic Ascaill, master-fitter of Obair-dhubhain Seann Skell, signs the lamp-makers' petition to the guild court as the one who drew the burner, and Joe Ashby, fitter, of Caol mhòr, signs under her. The guild's master carries the petition to the court the same afternoon.
